title: Chess in the Midst of Rebellion
body: In the early 1280s, King Alfonso X of Castile faced a heartbreaking rebellion led by his own son, Sancho. While sick and trapped in his palace in Seville, the king found solace in compiling knowledge. During this chaotic time, he finished his famous book of games, which became one of Europe's earliest and most beautiful guides to chess.

variants.lucy: Long ago in the 1280s, a king named Alfonso was very sick and could not leave his castle in Seville. While there was trouble outside, he sat quietly and gathered all the chess secrets he knew. He turned them into a beautiful book of games to keep his mind peaceful.
variants.luca: Talk about a family showdown! King Alfonso's own son led a rebellion against him, trapping the poor king inside his own palace. But instead of giving up, the king spent his time writing down the ultimate chess strategies. It became one of the very first and most famous game books in Europe.

source.author: Alfonso X (Castilla), ed. Raúl Orellana Calderón
